key_insight: A local hybrid pipeline combining a small language model with regular expressions can accurately extract uncoded urinary tract infection features from Catalan primary care notes without sending data to the cloud.
clinical_relevance: This approach could help turn free-text EHR narratives into usable structured data for research and quality improvement while better preserving privacy.
method: Deployed the open-weight Phi4-mini model inside the institutional firewall using Ollama.
Refined prompts with clinicians and added deterministic regular expressions after model output.
Validated on both real clinician-reviewed records and noisy synthetic notes designed to stress-test the pipeline.
evidence_signal: In 15,498 MEAP narratives from 2,962 patients, the pipeline found 4,663 feature occurrences and achieved 93.8% accuracy in real-world clinician validation.
watch_item: Performance was strong, but the approach still needs careful local calibration and oversight because multilingual notes, noisy text, and feature-specific errors can affect reliability.
paper_title: Uncoded Clinical Features from Multilingual Electronic Health Records in Catalonia: Development and Validation Study
